::: {.qs-footnote-note}
**Authoring and inclusion note.** Teaching repositories are independent scholarly resources, not folders copied into the personal website. Actual courses, classes, workshops, or training activities use `type-training`; the reusable Scientific Training Template uses `type-template`. New lesson material should normally use Quarto (`.qmd`), while notebooks and executable code remain appropriate when they serve the learning objective. A teaching repository may publish its own Quarto site under `qselmer.github.io/<repository>/`. Inclusion requires a defensible learning purpose or sequence, sufficient documentation, explicit provenance and attribution, and a canonical public source. Practice repositories, clones, copied tutorials, and partially adapted external material are not presented as authored teaching activities until their pedagogical structure and provenance are clear.
:::
